reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need the order list to see which customers are in this batch. I'll check orders first, then verify the refunds against the ledger.
The orders list shows acme, birch, and cobalt. Before paying, I'll check the refund ledger to confirm W2's claimed refunds were actually applied.
The refund ledger matches W2's handoff exactly (orders 292, 294, 295), so the refunds are confirmed. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 40355, which is 4834 + 35521 = 40355 with no refunds, consistent with the ledger. Next I'll check birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 40935 matches the expected figure: orders 291 and 294 total 51183, less the 10248 refund on order 294. Next I'll check cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt's balance of 29431 matches the ledger: orders 292 and 295 total 37699, less refunds 2929 and 5339 (8268), gives 29431. All three balances check out, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 40355 recorded successfully. Birch's balance of 40935 matches orders 291 and 294 less the 10248 refund, so I'll record that payout next.
Birch's payout of 40935 is recorded. Cobalt's balance of 29431 matches orders 292 and 295 (37699) less refunds 2929 and 5339, so I'll record that payout as the last one.
All three payouts recorded successfully and each matches the expected order total minus refunds: acme 40355, birch 40935, cobalt 29431. Finishing the batch.
